subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw expose a core shell/admin Gateway API for visible notifications to all connected Control UI sessions, and what auth scope, targeting, payload, and rate-limit rules should it use?
rationale: This is not a narrow bug repair: it creates a new shell-facing admin broadcast and user-interruption surface that current Gateway broadcast guards intentionally fail closed unless an event contract is defined.

options.title: Design the core contract first
options.body: Define a typed admin-scoped Gateway notification RPC/event, CLI shape, Control UI renderer, and abuse controls before assigning implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader notification architecture
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/20237 the product-design hub while keeping this issue as the shell/admin API requirement.

options.title: Route to plugin/API design
options.body: Defer a core command until maintainers decide whether plugins should get a public notification API instead of a built-in CLI feature.

recommendation.title: Design the core contract first
recommendation.body: Define a typed admin-scoped Gateway notification RPC/event, CLI shape, Control UI renderer, and abuse controls before assigning implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans product direction and security boundaries, and this account has recent adjacent Notification-settings history plus maintainer-routing context.
